hero: Saring is a jury for prediction-market disputes that can't rule on markets it bet on.
Saring: a jury for prediction-market disputes that can't rule on markets it bet on.
In 834 of 4,121 Polymarket disputes on UMA, a voter held a position in that market. Nothing filters them.
In 834 of 4,121 UMA disputes (20.2%), a voter held a position in that market. Nothing filters them.
case: Here is a real Panta market on Solana mainnet. Its details come from Panta's API, its holders from Panta's program.
A real Panta market on Solana mainnet: details from Panta's API, holders read from Panta's program.
Five jurors are real Panta wallets. God view, local to this demo, shows that three of them hold this market.
5 jurors are real Panta wallets. God view (local to this demo): 3 of them hold this market.
seat: You are juror number six, with your own secret ballot key. I vote NO, and also bet on NO.
You are juror #6, with your own secret ballot key. Vote NO, and also bet 0.01 SOL on NO.
The burner wallet gets devnet SOL. One full run costs about a tenth of a SOL.
Burner wallet funded with devnet SOL. One run costs about 0.10 SOL.
run: Now, 28 real devnet transactions on Arcium MPC, shown eight times faster. Every step links its transaction and its verified callback.
28 devnet transactions on Arcium MPC. Every step links its queue tx and its verified callback.
Positions are mirrored encrypted. A bribed juror rotates his key, so the briber's stale-key ballot is ignored inside MPC, and so is a forged one.
Positions mirrored encrypted. A bribed juror rotates his key: the briber's stale-key ballot and a forged one are ignored inside MPC.
verdict: The verdict, read from chain: NO, two to zero. Four excluded: the three conflicted holders, and me, because I bet.
Verdict: NO 2–0. 4 excluded: the 3 conflicted holders and you, because you bet.
A plain jury would have ruled YES. The market in the same program pays out on Saring's verdict.
A plain jury would have ruled YES. The market in the same program pays out on the verdict.
privacy: On chain there are only ciphertexts and four numbers: yes, no, excluded, and incomplete.
On chain: ciphertexts and four numbers (yes, no, excluded, incomplete).
explorer: Every step is a real devnet transaction you can open on the explorer.
Every step is a real devnet transaction on Solana Explorer.
multichain: The court stays on Solana and Arcium. Other chains pay for it, feed it data, or consume its verdict. Every card is a live read.
The court stays on Solana + Arcium. Other chains pay for it, feed it, or consume its verdict. Every card is a live read.
Tempo takes a paid dispute and settles a market with a Wormhole VAA. Zcash holds shielded juror bonds and slashes a no-show.
Tempo: paid dispute, market settled by Wormhole VAA. Zcash: shielded juror bonds, a no-show slashed.
On Arbitrum, a UMA dispute and a Kleros V2 ruling follow the verdict. On Base, Reality.eth, and a court seated from Limitless holders.
Arbitrum: UMA dispute + Kleros V2 ruling follow the verdict. Base: Reality.eth + a Limitless-holder court.
court: Anyone can audit a verdict. This public proof page traces one court from Solana, through its Wormhole VAA, to the chain that settled on it.
Public proof page: one court traced Solana → Wormhole VAA → the settle tx on the chain that used it.
